results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 39 aligned units' summaries match the controlling ideas of their spec paragraphs in spec order (p01-p39); the three opening callouts (IN THIS CHAPTER, KEY POINTS, FAILURE PATTERNS) are house-format blocks with no spec paragraph. Units 4 and 28 are summarized briefly but in line with p02 and p26.

Introduction callout (KEY POINTS): three bullets are the house-format synthesis block required by the book; each bullet supports the thesis (share not capacity, figures are load, late not failed), so it is not a paragraph with two controlling ideas.

In Practice at Larkfield: Eighteen Hours on Purpose ¶4: the second phrase (slower pace eases webhook load) supports the controlling idea 'the long run costs a later charge and nothing else' and is part of p31's declared controlling idea.
What to Take Away ¶1: a declared list (p35 'Established'); the capacity bullet is one of the established facts the list exists to gather, not a second controlling idea.
What to Take Away ¶3: a declared list (p37 'The author's synthesis'); its three bullets are the three parts of the one author's position the spec names.

results.draft_locus: How Each Provider Gets Its Capacity ¶4
results.quote: We periodically load test this system with merchants who hold transactions and then release the transactions in bulk
results.finding: The paragraph traces to S3 but contradicts its wording: S3 says 'no Adyen account of load testing, a peak freeze or payment rate limits was found', while the draft (correctly per AC-4, how_why and the section's controlling idea) quotes Adyen's documented load tests and code freeze. The draft is right; S3 is stale and should be corrected to say only that no Adyen payment rate limit or capacity figure was found. The same applies to the third 'Established' bullet.

Every other unit ties to a supporting claim: profiles to S1; figures to S2; capacity and near miss to S3; fairness, share, backpressure and downstream to S4; designs, Larkfield run and failure modes to S5; callouts and conclusion to the thesis as a whole.

results.draft_locus: How Each Provider Gets Its Capacity ¶1
results.quote: better balancing "gives us 15–20% more headroom before traffic bursts overwhelm the machines"
results.finding: The paragraph strings four Stripe quotations (AWS, shard splitting, synthetic load at 20x, proxy headroom) and ends on the last quote with no sentence saying what they show together (capacity rented and reshaped, partly still being built; the headroom remark is a dated statement and not a capacity figure). Flow-A also found the section's purpose for the integrator unclear until its last sentence. Add one closing sentence stating what the evidence shows.

All other tables, figures and quotations are followed (or, for figures, captioned) by a sentence saying what they show: Figure 1-4 captions; peak-profile table ('Those three properties decide...'); figures table ('These figures cannot be ranked'); Adyen capacity quotes (the '20x are different things' note and the inference callout); near-miss quote; peak-season quotes ('Neither company publishes its capacity'); error-low-level quote ('No bank was asked'); paths table (announced with its rule); designs table (p24); mock quote; comparison table (p27); backoff quote ('Spread your retries').

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary: e.g. p06 contrast ('accepted his arithmetic and disputed what it compared'), p08 cause_effect ('Those three properties decide what can be done'), capacity contrast ('The capacity behind those figures'), fairness cause_effect ('Since capacity is not published'), p22 similarity ('one more limit downstream, and it is yours'), designs problem_solution ('With a share per customer, backpressure and downstream limits in view'), p27 cause_effect ('So on Stripe'), p39 problem_solution ('Pacing leaves one problem open'). Openings of definition paragraphs (peak profile, backpressure) carry over through the preceding sentence and heading.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Larkfield: The Black Friday Objection ¶1
results.quote: In April 2027 a review of Keel, Larkfield's 2027 program to put its payments estate in order, reached decision K5
results.finding: Both readers had to stop and rebuild the timeline (1 October 2026 refusal, 1 November 2026 double charge, Femke since January 2027, April 2027 review, sources accessed November 2026) and the unexplained K-numbering (K5 here, K1 in When It Goes Wrong). Give the sequence once in the scene and say K5/K1 are numbered Keel decisions.

results.draft_locus: How Each Provider Gets Its Capacity ¶1
results.quote: That 2024 post says its platform
results.finding: 'That 2024 post' refers to a source named only inside the bold evidence-age bracket, so both readers re-read to find it; the load-test definition also arrives sentences before any load test.

results.draft_locus: How Each Provider Gets Its Capacity ¶3
results.quote: Capacity was not the weak point in the one peak-season near miss I found from either company.
results.finding: Both readers found the near-miss paragraph (and, for B, the freeze paragraph) out of place in a section about obtaining capacity; its purpose only becomes clear in the hand-off. A suggests putting it after the freeze paragraph, B moving it toward the hand-off. The order is the spec's (p14 before p15 inside 'capacity'); the prose could also say at the start why a change incident belongs here.

results.draft_locus: Four Ways to Meet a Predictable Peak ¶1
results.quote: Two rows are attested.
results.finding: Neither reader could tell which two rows were meant or what the other two rest on; the sentence should name the calendar and higher-ceiling rows.

results.draft_locus: Stripe and Adyen: Where They Differ ¶1

Either cite these in the body or drop the claim (or the cells).

results.draft_locus: Downstream Limits: Issuers and Networks ¶1
results.quote: Visa's rules put the underlying response code 91
results.finding: Response code 91 appears without being tied to issuer-unavailable; say that 91 is the code behind those declines.

results.draft_locus: The Share You Are Given: Fairness and Backpressure ¶3
results.quote: a refusal, a slower answer or an issuer-unavailable decline
results.finding: Figure 3's caption uses issuer-unavailable declines before the next section introduces the issuer (bolded there as a new term).
The introduction opens on a puzzling scenario (published peaks of 152,000 and 199,000 a minute against a refused run of about a thousand a minute); none of the weak patterns.
The conclusion sorts what is established, what depends on context and the author's position; it opens with no 'in conclusion', adds no new subtopic, and does not end on a restated thesis alone.

It joins the sections into one position no section states alone (plan against the share, not the figure; the October 7,900 were late while the November 1,840 were wrong and only the second cost refunds) and says why it matters: accept a longer run to send no wrong message.

Calls back to both named elements: 'Daniel's 152,000 a minute was everyone's traffic; the first of the month is yours alone' and 'The 7,900 renewals of October were late; the 1,840 of November were wrong'.

The cold reader predicted all ten roadmap sections in order, the evidence (dated provider documents, press figures, ledger numbers) and the sober, sceptical tone. Unknowns (the objection's wording, the names of the profiles and designs) are details the body supplies.

The reader predicts refusals at the account's share (100/s, 25/s per endpoint, 50 in progress) long before capacity, paces under the limit, backs off with random delay, resends under the same idempotency key and does not tell customers a rate-limited payment failed: matches expected.
The reader declines to rank: 'transaction' undefined, Adyen's figure likely includes in-person payments, both are reported load not capacity: matches expected.

In Practice uses 38% of monthly renewals in the first six hours, about 357,000 renewals, 7,900 delayed on 1 October 2026, and shows the job paced over 18 hours under K5 with the arithmetic for each provider.

The chapter states Adyen's periodic load tests with merchants, the code freeze around named peak days and utilization 'generally less than 30%', says no Adyen payment rate limit or capacity figure was found, and states 'It is not evidence about Adyen's capacity or about how Adyen divides it'; the comparison table keeps that line ('A difference in publication, not in capacity').
